title: Pars Plana Vitrectomy: Core Vitrectomy vs. Vitreous Base Shaving
summary: A comprehensive surgical reference guide contrasting central vitreous debulking (Core Vitrectomy) with peripheral vitreous clearance (Base Shaving). Critical for mastering microincisional vitrectomy surgery (MIVS), mitigating PVR risks, and preventing intraoperative iatrogenic retinal tears.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Anatomical Overview
sections.content:
Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) is broadly categorized into two fundamental phases: Core Vitrectomy and Vitreous Base Shaving. • Core Vitrectomy: The rapid debulking of the central 80% of the vitreous body (anterior hyaloid face, central core, and mid-periphery) to relieve anteroposterior traction, clear media opacities, and allow access to the retina.
• Vitreous Base Shaving: The meticulous removal of the dense peripheral vitreous gel adherent to the vitreous base—a 3 to 4 mm wide circumferential zone straddling the ora serrata (1.5–2.0 mm anterior and 2.0–3.0 mm posterior). Shaving requires wide-field visualization, dynamic scleral depression, high cut rates, and low linear vacuum to mitigate tractional forces on the peripheral retina.

references.citation: Adamo GG, Pellegrini M, Talli PM, Mondin R, Cartabellotta A, Giannaccare G, Mura M.. EPIRETINAL PROLIFERATION EMBEDDING WITHOUT INTERNAL LIMITING MEMBRANE PEELING FOR LAMELLAR MACULAR HOLE.. 2026

sections.title: Anatomy of the Vitreous Base & Insertion Site Dynamics

branches: Extent: 3-4 mm straddling the Ora Serrata
Adherence: Dense attachment to non-pigmented ciliary epithelium & ILM
Collagen Composition: High density Type II & Type IX collagen fibrils
Anterior Border: Just behind ciliary processes (Pars Plana)
Posterior Border: 2-3 mm posterior to Ora Serrata
Pathology Risk: Site of dynamic traction, retinal tears, PVR proliferation

sections.title: Step-by-Step Surgical Protocol: Core Vitrectomy Execution
content: Step 1: Trocar Placement: Insert 23G/25G/27G valved trocars at 3.5mm (phakic) or 3.0mm (pseudophakic) from limbus at a 30-degree bevel angle.
Step 2: Infusion Verification: Confirm infusion cannula tip is clearly within the vitreous cavity before turning on balanced salt solution (BSS).
Step 3: Central Debulking: Position vitreotome in central vitreous space facing away from the crystalline lens. Engage 5,000-10,000 CPM and linear 300-400 mmHg vacuum.
Step 4: PVD Induction: If posterior hyaloid is unattached, use active cutter suction (100-200 mmHg) or soft-tip cannula over optic nerve head to induce Posterior Vitreous Detachment.
Step 5: Mid-Periphery Clearance: Extend core removal peripherally until uniform red reflex is achieved and mid-peripheral traction is eliminated.

references.citation: Pérez González D.. A Standardized 10-Step Algorithm for Vitrectomy in Diabetic Tractional Retinal Detachment.. 2025

sections.title: Step-by-Step Surgical Protocol: Vitreous Base Shaving
content: Step 1: Chromovitrectomy Staining: Instill 0.1-0.2 mL of Preservative-Free Triamcinolone Acetonide (TRIESENCE/Kenalog) to coat and visualize vitreous fibrils.
Step 2: Dynamic Indentation: Apply dynamic scleral depression at the limbus/pars plana to bring peripheral vitreous base into direct viewing field.
Step 3: Parameter Adjustment: Increase cut rate to absolute maximum (e.g., 10,000-20,000 CPM) and drop vacuum to 50-150 mmHg to shorten sphere of influence.
Step 4: Port Orientation: Rotate vitrectomy probe port PARALLEL or AWAY from underlying retina; trim vitreous over sclerotomy sites and 360° periphery.
Step 5: Inspection: Re-evaluate 360° vitreous base under wide-field view and depression to identify and treat any subclinical retinal breaks with endolaser/cryotherapy.

references.citation: Pérez González D.. A Standardized 10-Step Algorithm for Vitrectomy in Diabetic Tractional Retinal Detachment.. 2025

sections.title: Instrumentation & Fluidics Dynamics
content: Sphere of Influence: Decreases exponentially with higher cut rates. High CPM (>10,000) limits pulsatile retinal traction during base shaving.
Port Alignment: Maintain vitreotome mouth parallel to the retinal surface to prevent suction engagement of mobile peripheral retina.
Dual-Pneumatic Cutters: Allow independent control of duty cycle, enabling 'Shutter-closed' duty cycles during shaving to restrict flow surge.
Gauge Selection: 27-Gauge probes provide enhanced stability near peripheral retina due to smaller port sizes and lower surge volumes.
Chandelier Illumination: Dual-fiber chandelier endoillumination frees both hands for bimanual dynamic scleral depression and cutter manipulation.

references.citation: Nagpal M, Juneja R, Talati S.. Managing PVR in the Era of Small Gauge Surgery.. 2021

sections.title: Intraoperative Chromovitrectomy Visualization Agents
content: Triamcinolone Acetonide (TA): Gold standard for base shaving. Suspension particles entrain within the vitreous matrix, turning transparent vitreous base into a distinct white cotton-like mass.
Brilliant Blue G (BBG): Selective for Internal Limiting Membrane (ILM); limited utility for vitreous base visualization.
Trypan Blue (0.15%): Excellent for Epiretinal Membrane (ERM) and anterior capsule staining; secondary stain for hyaloid face.
Fluorescein Sodium: Off-label liquid visualization of anterior hyaloid face and retrolental vitreous in pediatric phakic eyes.

references.citation: Russell JF, Boyce TM, De Melo Haefeli L, Russell SR, Meyering EE, Lang MJ, Goeken AA, Han IC, Tucker BA.. A Porcine Model of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Repair With Pars Plana Vitrectomy and Silicone Oil Tamponade.. 2026

rows: High vacuum or low cut rate engaging mobile, non-detached retina at vitreous base
Max cut rate (>10,000 CPM), low vacuum (<100 mmHg), keep port parallel to retina. Treat break with endolaser + gas/oil tamponade.
Inadvertent anterior cutter extension during 360° anterior vitreous base trimming
In phakic eyes, avoid aggressive anterior shaving unless imperative. Maintain visualization of probe tip relative to posterior capsule.
Incomplete shaving leaving vitreous flaps that tract during gas bubble movement
Perform complete 360° shaving of vitreous base; apply prophylactic 360° laser retinopexy in high-risk eyes (e.g., GRT, high myopia).
Excessive or violent scleral depression over pars plicata causing vascular tear
Apply gentle, controlled scleral indentation; avoid direct pressure on ciliary body processes. Maintain adequate IOP.

references.citation: Pérez González D.. A Standardized 10-Step Algorithm for Vitrectomy in Diabetic Tractional Retinal Detachment.. 2025

sections.title: Critical Intraoperative Emergency Red Flags
content: Sudden entrapment of retina into cutter port during vitreous base shaving (IMMEDIATE ACTION: Release foot pedal to zero vacuum; do NOT pull cutter away).
Rapid intraoperative eye softening or hypotony caused by sclerotomy leakage or infusion line dislodgement.
Unintentional lens touch causing acute posterior capsule rupture or instant lens opacification.
Dynamic expansion of a Giant Retinal Tear fold backward over the macula during fluid-air exchange due to residual anterior traction.
Suprachoroidal hemorrhage presenting as rapid shallowing of anterior chamber and dark peripheral choroidal elevations.

references.citation: Pérez González D.. A Standardized 10-Step Algorithm for Vitrectomy in Diabetic Tractional Retinal Detachment.. 2025

sections.title: Mnemonic for Vitreous Base Shaving Safety: S.H.A.V.E.

content.explanation:
S = Scleral Depression mandatory 360°
H = High Cut Rate (>10,000 CPM) & Low Vacuum (<150 mmHg)
A = Align Cutter Port Parallel/Away from underlying retina
V = Visualize with Triamcinolone Acetonide (TRIESENCE)
E = Examine 360° periphery for hidden breaks post-shave

references.citation: Damato B.. Progress in the management of patients with uveal melanoma. The 2012 Ashton Lecture.. 2012

sections.title: Pediatric & Special Population Considerations
sections.content:
• Pediatric Patients (ROP, FEVR, Trauma): The vitreoretinal adhesion is extremely strong. PVD cannot be safely induced by vacuum alone; automated vitreous cutter-assisted dissection at the vitreous base is required. Sclerotomies must be placed closer to the limbus (1.5–2.5 mm) depending on age to avoid pars plana/retinal detachment.
• High Myopes (> -6.00D or Axial Length >26.5mm): Thin sclera and staphyloma formation increase perforation risk during dynamic scleral depression. Extreme care is needed; lower indentation forces and lower vacuum parameters are mandatory during vitreous base shaving.
• Pseudophakic/Aphakic Eyes: Lack of crystalline lens support allows anterior hyaloid prolapse. Complete anterior vitreous base clearing is required to prevent vitreous wick syndrome or IOL capture.

references.citation: Russell JF, Boyce TM, De Melo Haefeli L, Russell SR, Meyering EE, Lang MJ, Goeken AA, Han IC, Tucker BA.. A Porcine Model of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Repair With Pars Plana Vitrectomy and Silicone Oil Tamponade.. 2026

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Evidence & Advances
content: PVR Prevention Studies: Incomplete vitreous base clearance is identified as the #1 operative cause for PVR scaffold formation and secondary RRD recurrence.
Dual-Blade & Bevel-Cutters: Bi-blade cutters (e.g., HYPERVIT, Unity) effectively double the cut rate up to 20,000 CPM, eliminating port flow turbulence and enabling safer base shaving.

Chandelier-Assisted Bimanual Shaving: Landmark VR surgical trials demonstrate a 40% reduction in iatrogenic break rates when bimanual dynamic scleral indentation is performed under chandelier illumination.

references.citation: Hussein MHMM, Seif ATS, Shaheen MHAEG, Mohalhal IA.. Macular micro vascular changes following macular hole repair: optical coherence tomography angiography study.. 2026

sections.title: High-Yield Clinical Pearls for VR Surgeons & Fellows
content: Core vs. Base Transition: Never begin base shaving until core vitrectomy is 100% complete. Residual central gel creates unwanted dynamic drag on peripheral structures.
The Triamcinolone Test: If you inject TA and see mobile white floating strands near the ora serrata, vitreous base shaving is incomplete. Continue shaving until the periphery is clear.
Infusion Pressure Management: Ensure IOP is maintained at 30-40 mmHg during scleral depression to avoid global collapse or hypotony-induced choroidal congestion.
Direction of Cutter: Always cut peripheral vitreous moving parallel to the circumferential vitreous base ribbon—never pull perpendicularly away from the retina.
